newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BORO HOPE FOR THIRD-TIME-LUCKY AGAINST LEICESTER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BORO HOPE FOR THIRD-TIME-LUCKY AGAINST LEICESTER.

text.p: Weary Middlesbrough aim to put two consecutive dispiriting cup-ties behind them and make it third time lucky when they face Leicester in the English League Cup final replay on Wednesday.

Boro enter the tie at neutral Hillsborough just three days after their dramatic F.A. Cup semifinal against second division Chesterfield and 10 days after their energy-sapping first clash with Leicester on the wide open spaces of Wembley.

Both matches went to extra time and both times Middlesbrough, still searching for the first major trophy of their 121-year history, had to settle for stalemate after conceding agonisingly late equalisers.
The resulting replays have snarled up their late-season premier league programme and could seriously jeapordise their chances of league survival.

But Boro will have to put the threat of relegation out of their minds once again on Wednesday if they are to beat a stubborn Leicester side who have proved their fighting qualities time and again this season.

Boro came through Sunday's Old Trafford 3-3 epic against Chesterfield unscathed and their foreign legion of Juninho, Emerson, Fabrizio Ravanelli, Gianluca Festa and Mikkel Beck are all expected to start.

Club captain Nigel Pearson, who missed the Chesterfied match though injury, faces a late fitness test, and highly-rated Australian goalkeeper Mark Schwarzer, who was cup-tied on Sunday, is almost certain to return.

Leicester's American goalkeeper Kasey Keller is facing a fitness battle, as are captain Steve Walsh, defender Simon Grayson and midfielder Gary Parker. Manager Martin O'Neill will wait until the last minute before naming his team.

Leicester, who still have relegation worries of their own, are expected to employ similar spoiling tactics to those which earned them a 1-1 draw in the first match at Wembley, with Swedish international Pontus Kaamark shadowing Juninho at every step.

The Brazilian, who was in breathtaking form on Sunday, is desparate to guide Boro into Europe through one of the domestic cup competitions, and has hinted he might leave the club if they fail to get there.
"If we get into Europe I'm definitely staying here, if we don't qualify I don't know," he said. "I have two seasons left on my contract and I'll have to wait and see."
While Middlesbrough and Leicester lock horns in Sheffield, title-chasing Liverpool face neighbours Everton in a league match at Goodison Park.

Liverpool put their championship bid back on track with a 2-1 win at Sunderland on Sunday and victory in the highly-charged Merseyside derby would take them level on points with leaders Manchester United, who they face in a potential title-decider at Anfield on Saturday.

"We have to play our two hardest fixtures of the year in the space of three days," Liverpool's England international Steve McManaman said. "We have to beat both Everton and United if we're to stand any chance.
"Everton on Wednesday will be a scrap, then comes United. All we can do is look after ourselves and prepare for a difficult week."
